assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of materials in which protected boundary states follow from bulk band topology. The theory of the quantum spin Hall state, its realisation in HgTe quantum wells and the three-dimensional topological insulators identified by photoemission together form a coherent discovery with very broad influence across condensed-matter physics, spectroscopy and device ideas. It is a clear case of discovery plus experimental realisation, which fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the decisive theory; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental quantum spin Hall observation; Hasan's group delivered early 3D topological insulator spectroscopy. Eugene Mele is a co-author of the key Kane-Mele papers, so leaving him out is a real allocation cost; the three-person limit forces a choice, and I favour the theory-plus-two-experiments balance. Others (Zhang, Bernevig, Fu) are outside the supplied credited names and I cannot assign them here.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation in many materials and techniques, including ARPES, transport and STM. The interpretation is stable and the field is mature; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp and Hasan, and relative to theorists not on the credited list, is contested.
I am relying on memory of the priority sequence and have not independently verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created the twistronics field. It is a conceptually new and original route to tunable strongly correlated physics in a single, clean, controllable material, with large downstream impact on moire materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key continuum-model prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting phases. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment prize configuration. Cory Dean, Pablo's collaborators and others contributed to related moire work but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups worldwide within a few years, and the stack of moire platforms is now broad. Open questions on the origin of the superconductivity remain, but the discovery itself is secure. Timely and probably near the point of maturity.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in the system is unsettled, so the prize would rest on the discovery of the phases and flat bands, not an explanation.
Reproducibility depends on sample twist-angle disorder; I have not verified details of priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, have reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and now underpin precision tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. This is an invention with a clear, quantifiable measurement impact and many downstream uses.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first realisations; Jun Ye's group pushed the strontium clock to record accuracy and stability and developed the many-body and comb-linked tools. A two-person prize is well supported by the supplied credit. Other groups (NIST, PTB, others) contributed, and I leave the wider field aside.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across many laboratories and species; accuracies are well established. The field is mature and the application path is clear, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs and ion clocks may be weighed by the committee.
Whether the committee views this as a distinct invention or as an incremental refinement of earlier clock physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics allows strong, controllable coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave photons and is the architecture behind most superconducting quantum processors. It is original, concrete and has major instrument impact on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators supplied the theory proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf and colleagues realised strong coupling in the first experiments. The three-person configuration is plausible, though Devoret and Martinis, honoured recently for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, are outside this credited list and the committee may regard the topic as partially covered.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and now an industrial platform. The concept is stable; timing is acceptable, though recent circuit-related prizing could weigh against it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the most recent prize for superconducting circuits and an uncertain boundary between the topics.
Allocation relative to other founders of circuit-based qubits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature giant tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, then the large effect in MgO barriers, enabled modern magnetic read heads and MRAM. It is a materials-and-interface physics advance with strong scientific and technological results; the interface structure and spin-dependent tunnelling are close to my own area of electron microscopy of interfaces.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995; Yuasa (and Parkin, who is not on the supplied list) demonstrated the large MgO-based effect. The three listed names can form a fair configuration but credit relative to Parkin is a genuine open issue. I note that the 2007 prize was already given for GMR.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by decades of research and commercial use. Recognition is mature, if somewhat late relative to the field's early advances.
uncertainties: Absence of Stuart Parkin from the credited names makes the MgO story incomplete.
Relationship to the 2007 GMR prize could count against distinctiveness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The insulated-gate bipolar transistor combined MOS gate control with bipolar conduction, and became the workhorse of power electronics, with large energy-efficiency effects across motors, rail and grids. This is a clear invention with enormous practical impact, the kind of device achievement the physics prize has honoured before.
assessment.attribution: Baliga is the single credited name and is widely associated with the concept and its development at GE; others in industry (for example Japanese and other developers) also contributed device versions, and I cannot resolve that from the list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and clear technological maturity; recognition would be very late but fully secure.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this physics or engineering.
Attribution disputes with other IGBT developers cannot be settled from the supplied material.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The qPlus sensor and CO-functionalised tips give atomic-resolution force microscopy and the imaging of the internal bond structure of single molecules. It is a genuine instrumental invention that changed how surfaces and molecules are imaged, and as a microscopist I regard the method's reach as high, though narrower than the larger condensed-matter candidates.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor; Meyer and Gross demonstrated the molecular bond-resolved imaging with functionalised tips. The three-name configuration seems natural, but wider contributions from other scanning-probe groups are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and used by many groups; the technique is mature, although the physics is more tool-focused and the community reach smaller than for several competitors.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the impact large enough compared with fundamental discoveries.
Overlap with the earlier scanning-probe prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube detected a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later evidence for a blazar and the Galactic plane as sources, establishing neutrino astronomy. It is a discovery enabled by a large new instrument, with strong significance.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Karle was a leading experimental figure; the large collaboration is hard to represent in a three-person limit, and the supplied credit is narrow.
assessment.maturity: Observed with high significance and cross-checked, but source identification is still developing and the physics interpretation is evolving.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within a very large collaboration.
The source picture remains incomplete, so maturity could be questioned.
